To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ArgJ gene codes for a bifunctional acetylornithine-glutamate N acetyltransferase, and that this enzyme is involved in the arginine acetyl cycle.

(i) the argJ gene coding the N2-acetylL-ornithine:L-glutamate N-acyltransferase has been cloned from three thermophilic microorganism; (ii) archaeal ArgJ is a monofunctionnal enzyme, whereas bacterial ArgJ are bifuncional enzymes; (iii) the catalytic mechanism follows a ping-pong bi bi kinetic mechanism; (iv) the ArgJ enzymes from all three thermophillic organisms are synthesized as
the ArgJ gene coding for acetylornithine aminotransferase has been cloned from three thermophilic micro-organisms and the enzyme purified.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning, expression, characterization, and kinetic mechanism of monofunctional and bifunctional ArgJ from thermophilic organisms.
the characterization and kinetic mechanism of monofunctional and bifunctional enzymes involved in the arginine biosynthetic pathway of thermophilic micro-organisms.
the characterization of a key enzyme of L-arginin biosynthesis from thermophilic organisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acetyl cycle is a linear pathway in M. jannachii and that the pathway is closed in T. neapolitanus and B. steraothermophilus, where N2-acetylglutaminate is used to generate ornithine.

the ArgJ protein is the key enzyme in the acetyl pathway of L-argininine biosynthesis, and it is present as a monofunctionale or a bifunctional enzyme, the latter being a product of a single polypeptide chain.
the archaeal and bacterial enzymes are monofunctional and bifunctional respectively, but the catalytic mechanism of both is identical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the acetyl cycle for L-arginine in thermophilic microorganism is a key metabolic pathway for the production of this amino acid, which is an essential component of the peptidoglycan of the cell wall.

the acetyl cycle in thermophilic organisms is a linear pathway, in which the key enzyme ArgJ is bifunctional, whereas in mesophilic organisms this cycle is a cyclic pathway, in which ArgJ is monofunctional.

the acetylornithine cycle is a common pathway in all organisms, but the enzyme catalyzing the first step of this pathway, acetylornithinate: L-ornithinase (ArgE), is not a common enzyme, but is a bifunctional protein (Acetylglutamate kinase and acetylornithate: L-ornitinase) in thermophilic bacteria, and monofunctional in thermophilic archaea and in mesophilic bacteria
The main takeaway from our work is that
ArgJ enzymes from thermophilic organisms are bifunctional and that they follow ping-pong bi bi kinetic mechanism.
the acetyl cycle is present in all thermophilic microorganism studied to date.
bifunctional enzymes are more frequent in thermophilic micro-organisms, and that they are often encoded by a single gene.
